jurisdiction.name: Group of Twenty
jurisdiction.overview: Forum of 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union, with a rotating presidency and no secretariat. Its texts are political commitments.

narrative.summary: G20 trade and digital economy ministers adopted the G20 AI Principles in 2019. Digital ministers' declarations in 2020 (Riyadh), 2021 (Trieste) and 2024 (Maceió) each carry a dedicated AI section, the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration of 2023 has a section on harnessing AI responsibly, and G20 innovation ministers under the 2026 United States presidency adopted a statement with AI pillars and the G20 AI Prosperity Objectives.
narrative.review_notes: Membership is taken from Global Affairs Canada's G20 page, and the African Union's accession from the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration of 9-10 September 2023 on the same site, which gives no exact accession day; the AI Principles come from the Tsukuba ministerial statement published by Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. The Osaka Leaders' Declaration (June 2019) and later G20 statements on AI are still pending.

instruments.publisher_name: G20 Trade Ministers and Digital Economy Ministers (Japan 2019 presidency)
instruments.current_status: Annex to the G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy adopted at the G20 Ministerial Meeting in Tsukuba, Japan, on 8-9 June 2019. Paragraph 19 states the G20 AI Principles, drawn from the OECD Recommendation on AI, 'are non-binding'; the G20 supports the Section 1 principles and takes note of the Section 2 recommendations.
instruments.summary: Principles drawn from the OECD Recommendation on AI and welcomed by G20 trade and digital economy ministers in 2019. Section 1 sets five principles for responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI (inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being; human-centred values and fairness; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; accountability), which the G20 supports; Section 2 lists national-policy and international-cooperation recommendations, which the G20 takes note of. The text states that the principles are non-binding.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI principles endorsed at G20 ministerial level, extending the OECD AI Principles to G20 members that are not OECD adherents.
instruments.evidence_reference: Research pass 2026-10-21: Not re-read in this pass; no correction proposed. instruments.official_title: G20 Digital Economy Ministers Meeting – Ministerial Declaration
instruments.english_title: G20 Digital Economy Ministers' Declaration (Saudi Presidency, 2020), with Annex 1: Examples of National Policies to Advance the G20 AI Principles
instruments.summary: Declaration of G20 digital economy ministers under the Saudi presidency. Its first section, 'Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence', reaffirms a human-centred approach to AI and support for the G20 AI Principles; each member commits to advance the Principles in line with national priorities. It welcomes Annex 1, 'Examples of National Policies to Advance the G20 AI Principles', and calls for inclusive multi-stakeholder dialogue on AI. Other sections cover cross-border data flows, smart cities, measurement and security of the digital economy.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the G20 Ministers responsible for the digital economy, who met on 22 July 2020 under the Saudi G20 Presidency. Annex 1 states it is not meant to be prescriptive.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read the English PDF on the Saudi Ministry of Communications and IT site (2020 presidency host): date line 'Wednesday, July 22, 2020'; section I 'Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence'; Annex 1 named. Arabic version: https://www.mcit.gov.sa/sites/default/files/g20ss_declaration_g20_digital_economy_ministers_meeting_ar_0.pdf. Annex PDF: https://www.mcit.gov.sa/sites/default/files/examples-of-ai-national-policies.pdf (not opened). curl through the proxy was refused (403); WebFetch worked. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, date (22 July 2020), Saudi Presidency, Section I 'Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence', Annex 1 title and the 'commit to advance the G20 AI Principles, in accordance with national priorities' wording all confirmed on mcit.gov.sa PDF.; current_status: the document does not state it creates no legal obligations; Annex 1 only says it 'is not meant to be prescriptive'. instruments.official_title: Declaration of G20 Digital Ministers: Leveraging Digitalisation for a Resilient, Strong, Sustainable and Inclusive Recovery
instruments.english_title: Declaration of G20 Digital Ministers (Trieste, 2021), with Annex 1: G20 Policy Examples on How to Enhance the Adoption of AI by MSMEs and Start-ups
instruments.summary: Declaration of G20 digital ministers under the Italian presidency. Section ii, 'Leveraging Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for MSMEs' Inclusiveness and Start-ups' Promotion', reaffirms human-centred, trustworthy AI and the G20 AI Principles, notes low AI uptake among small firms, and commits to strengthening their AI capabilities (data, finance, skills) and to agile approaches such as regulatory sandboxes. Annex 1 sets out G20 policy examples for AI adoption by MSMEs and start-ups. Other sections cover digital government, children online, data flows and connectivity.
instruments.current_status: Declaration of G20 Digital Ministers dated 5 August 2021, Trieste, Italy (meeting held both physically and virtually), under the Italian G20 Presidency.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read the PDF linked from the Italian Department for Digital Transformation page (dated 05 August 2021). The PDF has no separate date line; text states the ministers met in Trieste on 5 August 2021. Section ii and Annex 1 confirmed. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, subtitle, date (5th of August 2021), Trieste, Italy, section ii title, regulatory sandboxes and Annex 1 title confirmed on the innovazione.gov.it PDF.; current_status: the text does not state that the declaration creates no legal obligations (only Annex 2 footnote says those Principles are not binding). The meeting was held both physically and virtually.

instruments.english_title: G20 Digital Economy Ministerial Declaration, Maceió (2024)
instruments.summary: Declaration of G20 digital economy ministers under the Brazilian presidency. Its section 'Artificial intelligence for inclusive sustainable development and inequality reduction' reaffirms the G20 AI Principles and the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, commits to risk-based, human-centric, development-oriented and innovation-friendly AI policy and governance approaches, calls for international cooperation and capacity building, acknowledges efforts to improve public services with AI, and notes the Toolkit for AI Readiness and Capacity Assessment presented by the Brazilian presidency with UNESCO support.
instruments.current_status: Declaration of the G20 Ministers responsible for the Digital Economy, who convened in Maceió, Brazil, on 13 September 2024 under the Brazilian presidency.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read the full text on GOV.UK (UK government, a G20 member; published 14 September 2024). The text states ministers convened in Maceió on 13 September 2024. The Brazilian presidency site (gov.br/g20) was not reachable in the first pass.
